claims.claim: NVIDIA’s SC26 presentation describes agents that can plan experiments, run code, and check results on researchers’ own systems.
claims.source_title: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents

claims.claim: NVIDIA says an Argonne National Laboratory agent accepted a prompt, planned and tested hypotheses, selected simulations, and identified two new binding sites.
claims.source_title: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents

claims.claim: Nemotron for Science combines Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with scientific evaluations, an open chemistry dataset, and post-training recipes for specialized science agents; NVIDIA says researchers can adapt the models for tasks including chemistry experiments and protein design.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA Introduces Nemotron for Science to Accelerate Discoveries With Agents

claims.claim: LitmusBench v0.2 contains nearly 50,000 chemistry questions for training and evaluation, including tasks related to molecular properties, drug-discovery data, solubility, and how the body processes molecules.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA Introduces Nemotron for Science to Accelerate Discoveries With Agents

claims.claim: NVIDIA reports that a KTH Royal Institute of Technology agent repaired broken GROMACS molecular-dynamics setups, fixing 81% of test cases in one overnight run; each fix was independently checked by GROMACS.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA Introduces Nemotron for Science to Accelerate Discoveries With Agents

claims.claim: The agent loop depends on tool use and evaluation between model steps: NVIDIA describes CPUs handling tool calls, operations, result gathering, and evaluation, while its agent-evaluation guidance says multi-step systems must be assessed through tool calls and task outcomes rather than a single text response.
claims.source_title: How to Evaluate AI Agents From Tool Calls to Task Completion

claims.claim: NVIDIA’s own scientific-agent material warns that verification can require computational or real-world data and may take hours or days, because a single mistake can derail a research task.
claims.source_title: How to Train Scientific Agents with Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: NVIDIA connects the SC26 infrastructure story to climate modeling and engineering: Vera is presented for climate, molecular, and engineering simulations, while Rubin HPC is described as accelerating simulations used to test candidate materials, molecules, and designs.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA Expands Vera CPU Platform to Accelerate Scientific Discovery
